![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14197487/assets/d652e7ffe301986acf3b5ed02c00cc775d5f9ec2e7849248b7478e90a2a4aacb.png)

The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[-2,2].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above, where the areas of the regions between the graph and the $x$-axis are $1$ and $5$ respectively (from left to right). Find the minimum value of $f(x)$ on the interval $[-2,2]$ given that $f(-2)=-5.$
question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates test, the minimum value of $f(x)$ on $[-2,2]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (-2,2),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at $x=-1.$ Therefore, the candidates are $x=-2,-1,2.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) & =-5 \\ f(-1) & =f(-2)+{\int }_{-2}^{-1}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5-1 \\  & =-6 \\ f(2) & =f(-2)+{\int }_{-2}^{2}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-5-1+5 \\  & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the smallest value of $f$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{f}_{\text{min}}=min\{-5,-6,-1\}=-6.
$$

Therefore, the minimum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{min}}=-6,$ and the value of $x$ that minimizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{min}}=-1.$
